title: The Space Between
theme: Openings, frames, cavities and the shaping of negative space
ordering: Chronological, based on the objects’ creation dates or identified publication dates for original digital works.
interpretation: Cross-cultural comparison, not a proposed single lineage of influence.

works.title: Female Head with Braided Hair
works.caption: c. 2000–1750 BCE. Beneath the modeled hair and face is a hollow channel, probably made to receive a stick or temporary stand. Here an unseen opening helps explain how the head may have been presented.

works.title: Stirrup-spout bottle with feline and snake
works.caption: 1200–800 BCE. Two branches join to form the vessel’s spout, enclosing an opening above the body. The Met suggests that this form may have served as a handle or reduced evaporation; its precise significance remains uncertain.

works.title: Vishnu with Eight Arms
works.caption: c. 600. The surviving arch and the god’s many arms divide the surrounding space into distinct openings. Turn the figure to see how the outer frame, body and attributes remain connected through the stone.

works.title: Incense Burner
works.caption: First half of the 13th century. Piercing gives the metal dome a double role: it carries ornament and opens the container to the air. The patterned gaps allow an interior associated with burning incense to communicate with the surrounding room.

works.title: Table Fountain
works.caption: c. 1320–1340. Arches and columns turn this fountain into a miniature building. Its open tiers are part of a larger spectacle: the museum records water wheels and bells that added movement and sound.

works.title: Thomas Cup
works.caption: 1690. The opening between the embracing animals is easy to see; the cup’s hidden channels are harder to understand. This drinking puzzle makes visible and concealed spaces work together, directing both the eye and the liquid.

works.title: Snake sitting on a skull
works.caption: 19th century. A snake coils over the hollows of a skull. The carver uses gaps and recesses to separate living body from bone while bringing both into one compact netsuke.

works.title: Cubic-Modular Wall Structure, Black
works.caption: 1966. The open grid makes the space within each square as regular as the painted wooden members around it. This digital reconstruction lets the viewer compare the repeated openings from an oblique angle.

works.title: Incomplete Open Cube 6/8
works.caption: 1974. Six edges suggest a cube whose missing members the viewer can mentally complete. The empty interior and the absent edges become central to the work. This model is a digital reconstruction after LeWitt’s aluminum structure.

works.title: Contemporary Female Figure
works.caption: c. 1990. Slender brass limbs leave broad openings around the torso and between the legs. Elaborate hair and small details remain legible within a figure whose silhouette depends on the surrounding space.

works.title: Two Reclining Figures on a Calder Base
works.caption: 2006–2018. Elongated bodies and a branching base turn the gaps between figures into an active part of the composition. As the model rotates, forms cross and separate. The original sculpture is blue; this archived model is uncolored.

works.title: Africhibi: Aimasai
works.caption: 2022 publication. Aimasai’s encircling arms create a large opening around the simplified body. Nairobi Design Week draws on Kenyan soapstone sculpture and jewelry to give a contemporary digital character its distinctive outline.
